meaning: to argue a position you don't necessarily hold, in order to test an idea
literal_translation: hacer de abogado del diablo: defender una postura contraria para poner a prueba una idea
example: Someone should play devil's advocate here, or we'll never see the flaws in this plan.
origin: From the Latin 'advocatus diaboli', the official in the Catholic Church who argued against a candidate's canonization

wrong_meanings.meaning: to refuse to take any side in a debate
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes arguing one side on purpose, not avoiding a position altogether.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to deceive an opponent with false evidence
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: Playing devil's advocate is an open exercise; the speaker openly tests an idea and does not hide it.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to accept an argument without questioning it
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the opposite of the idiom, which involves deliberately challenging an argument.

explanation: 'Play devil's advocate' means to argue against a position, usually as a deliberate test of its strength, even if you do not agree with it. It is common in meetings and academic discussions.
